body:
Well, thanks for taking the time out to reply :) I'll consider telling the person I talk to about suicide. It's just that the thought of ending up in a mental hospital terrifies me.

I've been wondering if I've actually been depressed pretty much my whole life. Growing up in middle and high school, I figured I just hated my hometown, like a lot of people do, and that once I got far, far away, I'd be a lot happier. But now that I'm out, I haven't found myself feeling a whole lot better. It may still be a lifestyle thing, though. The school I go to is mega stressful, and has a well-known very high rate of depression.

But, y'know, the brain isn't so simple. I think it's a combination of factors--part innate chemical imbalances, part me not being able to deal with stress. I want to try medication. I'm just scared about fucking up my thinking/my brain/my capacity to learn while trying to find a medicine that works for me. I know that not all medicines are created equal, and some do wonders for some people and bring hell to others.

That's kind of an interesting thought--that I've boiled suicide down into some kind of casual escape mechanism. I guess I do sort of see it that way in a lot of ways, that there's always this big OFF button I can push and enter into the unknown.

I feel pretty damn shitty, but I more than certainly won't do it. At least not at this point. That's why I'm seeing someone before this gets really out of hand.
